answer.answerText: No. The evidence establishes that ADR-042 constrained Story-0039's mode boundary, but not that it caused the persisted account identity or explicit PAPER provisioning. Those decisions are explicitly assigned to the separate Account Identity and Risk Facts ADR, ADR-043.

claims.text: ADR-042 explicitly requires a separate ADR for account identity and PAPER risk facts and states that these concerns are intentionally not hidden in ADR-042.

ADR-042 identifies the first implementation Story as Account Identity and PAPER Risk Facts only after ADR-042 and the separate identity/risk ADR are accepted, but does not identify Story-0039 by name.
Story-0039 attributes the independent account identities and canonical relation to ADR-043, while describing ADR-042 only as preserving the execution-mode boundary.

Story-0039 was implemented under both ADR-042 and ADR-043, so ADR-042 provided an architectural constraint, but the available evidence does not establish it as the causal source of the identity and provisioning requirements.
ADR-043 states that it provides the account identity and facts-source architecture needed to make ADR-042's mode distinction executable safely, without superseding ADR-042.

evidence.excerpt: A separate ADR is required before implementing the first PAPER risk/identity story... This is broader than position close and is intentionally not hidden in ADR-042.

No Engineering Story is created by this ADR. Once ADR-042 and the separate Account Identity/Risk Facts ADR are accepted, the first implementation Story should remain: Establish PAPER Account Identity and Risk Facts.
ADR-043 defines two independent identities... ADR-042 preserves the execution-mode boundary...
ADR-043 provides the account identity and facts-source architecture required to make that distinction executable safely. It does not supersede ADR-042.
ADR_042_CHANGED = NO; ADR_043_CHANGED = NO; NEW_ADR_REQUIRED = NO
